title: Energy Transition Skills: New Economy Skills Report | World Economic Forum
gist: The World Economic Forum's fourth New Economy Skills report argues that rising demand for energy, minerals and natural resources, amid geopolitical and climate pressure, makes the transition dependent on workforce skills. It finds demand for transition skills is growing and broadening across industries and regions while skill-development efforts are insufficient, and calls for reskilling existing workers and demand-led education.

themes.theme: Resource demand under geopolitical and climate stress

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum states that demand for energy, minerals and other natural resources is rising at the same time that geopolitical tensions and climate risks are adding pressure on resource systems.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Supports a structural-tightness view for energy and critical minerals, where demand growth meets supply-side geopolitical and climate disruption.
insights.quote: Demand for energy, minerals and other natural resources is rising, while geopolitical tensions and climate risks are placing additional pressure on these systems.
insights.locator: Demand for energy, minerals and other

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum frames more efficient, resilient and sustainable energy and resource systems as increasingly essential to economic growth and national competitiveness, not merely an environmental objective.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Signals policy framing of transition spending as a competitiveness and resilience priority, which tends to sustain public support for grid, efficiency and supply-chain investment.
insights.quote: More efficient, resilient and sustainable systems are increasingly essential to economic growth and competitiveness.
insights.locator: Demand for energy, minerals and other

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum argues that delivering the energy and resource transition depends on having workers with the right skills, making human capital a binding constraint on execution.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Labor and skills shortages can delay transition projects and raise their costs; monitor wage inflation and project timelines in clean-energy and grid build-outs.
insights.quote: Delivering this transition will depend on people with the skills to make it happen.
insights.locator: Demand for energy, minerals and other

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum's New Economy Skills report (fourth in the series) finds that demand for energy transition skills is growing and broadening across industries and regions, but efforts to develop those skills are insufficient.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A widening supply-demand gap for transition talent implies execution risk for developers and utilities and opportunity for training, staffing and engineering-services providers.
insights.quote: It finds that demand for transition skills is growing and broadening, but efforts to develop them are insufficient.
insights.locator: The fourth installment of the New

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum recommends closing the energy transition skills gap by building on workers' existing skills, aligning education and training more closely with real-world demand, and ensuring organizations of all sizes, not just large firms, can access needed skills.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Reskilling of adjacent workforces and demand-led training are the policy levers to watch; smaller firms are flagged as most at risk of being skill-constrained.
insights.locator: The fourth installment of the New
